paper.abstract: Nascent platforms for programmable quantum simulation offer unprecedented access to new regimes of far-from-equilibrium quantum many-body dynamics in almost isolated systems. Here achieving precise control over quantum many-body entanglement is an essential task for quantum sensing and computation. Extensive theoretical work indicates that these capabilities can enable dynamical phases and critical phenomena that show topologically robust methods to create, protect and manipulate quantum entanglement that self-correct against large classes of errors. However, so far, experimental realizations have been confined to classical (non-entangled) symmetry-breaking orders 1-5 . In this work, we demonstrate an emergent dynamical symmetry-protected topological phase 6 , in a quasiperiodically driven array of ten 171 Yb + hyperfine qubits in Quantinuum's System Model H1 trapped-ion quantum processor 7 . This phase shows edge qubits that are dynamically protected from control errors, cross-talk and stray fields. Crucially, this edge protection relies purely on emergent dynamical symmetries that are absolutely stable to generic coherent perturbations. This property is special to quasiperiodically driven systems: as we demonstrate, the analogous edge states of a periodically driven qubit array are vulnerable to symmetry-breaking errors and quickly decohere. Our work paves the way for implementation of more complex dynamical topological orders 8,9 that would enable error-resilient manipulation of quantum information.

# Evidence brief: Dumitrescu et al., *Nature* 2022 — DOI verification and experimental limitation

## Bottom line
- **DOI is verified.** The DOI 10.1038/s41586-022-04853-4 is confirmed by the publisher's own page.
- **No limitation from the original paper was obtained.** Neither the publisher full text nor the author manuscript was accessible, so I cannot give an exact supporting passage. I have not inferred or paraphrased one.

## 1. DOI verification

| Check | Result | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Publisher landing page | `https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-022-04853-4`. Same title and abstract text; published 2022-07-20. | Search-extracted text from nature.com |
| Europe PMC / MEDLINE record | PMID 35859195; same DOI; first publication 2022-07-20; not open access; not retracted. | Europe PMC REST record (receipt dated 2026-11-09T19:46:27Z) |
| Bibliographic details | *Nature* **607**, 463–467 (2022). | Reference lists of citing papers, e.g. PMC9709576 and https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-46402-9 |
| Preprint | arXiv:2107.09676, titled "Realizing a dynamical topological phase in a trapped-ion quantum simulator" (2021). | Cited as ref. 45 in the companion paper, doi:10.1038/s41586-022-04854-3. **I did not retrieve the preprint itself.** |

**Conclusion:** the Europe PMC DOI matches the publisher record. The preprint title differs slightly from the published title.

**Why the PubMed exact-title search returned zero:** this is unresolved. The record exists under PMID 35859195, so the miss is probably a query or indexing artefact, not a missing paper. I did not fetch the PubMed record directly.

## 2. Experimental limitation from the original text: not obtained

- `read_paper` returned **abstract only** (`fullTextStatus: not_available_from_open_access_service`).
- The nature.com result contained only abstract snippets.
- No passage from the article body, Methods, or arXiv:2107.09676 was retrieved.

**What the abstract itself implies:**
- It claims stability to *"generic coherent perturbations"*.
- It does not say whether the edges are protected against incoherent noise, such as decoherence or memory and depolarizing errors.
- That is a **question to check in the full text**, not a documented limitation.

## 3. Contrary and contextual evidence (not about the target paper's own limitations)

**Companion experiment, superconducting qubits** (doi:10.1038/s41586-022-04854-3, search-extracted snippets):
- Edge-spin oscillations show *"a gradually decaying envelope"*, attributed via an echo test to *"circuit errors rather than thermalization"*.
- The authors note that, *"because of the small system size and experimental imperfections… we are not able to observe the logarithmic entanglement growth"*.
- These limitations belong to that experiment, not to Dumitrescu et al.

**Review** (Nature Communications 2024, PMC10923891):
- It describes the quasiperiodic system as one that *"might prove to provide stable edge states robust against coherent errors"*, which is hedged language.
- Its statement that detecting *"the true long-range nature of the spatiotemporal order is still out-of-reach"* cites different references (84–86), not ref. 77 (Dumitrescu). It should **not** be attributed to the target paper.

## 4. Classification of what was found

- **Experimental findings (abstract level only):**
  - ten ¹⁷¹Yb⁺ hyperfine qubits on Quantinuum System Model H1;
  - quasiperiodic drive;
  - edge qubits protected against control errors, cross-talk and stray fields;
  - periodic-drive edges decohere quickly.
- **Theoretical claim:** the edges are "absolutely stable" to generic coherent perturbations through emergent dynamical symmetries. This is stated in the abstract; its experimental support is not verified here.
- **Not applicable:** binding sites and motif predictions, since this is a physics paper.

## 5. Access and coverage limits
- Coverage was abstract plus search snippets only; there was no full-text reading. This is not a systematic review.
- The search tools (Perplexity) are not independent confirmation of content. Europe PMC and PubMed draw on the same underlying record.

## 6. Next steps
1. Retrieve arXiv:2107.09676 directly (`https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.09676`). Read the discussion and Methods for:
   - the number of drive cycles achieved;
   - edge-signal decay from incoherent errors;
   - system size and finite-size effects;
   - error mitigation or post-selection.
2. Alternatively, obtain the *Nature* full text and Supplementary Information through institutional access.
3. Fetch the PubMed record for PMID 35859195 directly to resolve the zero-hit title search.

papers.title: Dynamical topological phase realized in a trapped-ion quantum simulator.
papers.authors: Dumitrescu PT, Bohnet JG, Gaebler JP, Hankin A, Hayes D, Kumar A, Neyenhuis B, Vasseur R, Potter AC.
papers.abstract: Nascent platforms for programmable quantum simulation offer unprecedented access to new regimes of far-from-equilibrium quantum many-body dynamics in almost isolated systems. Here achieving precise control over quantum many-body entanglement is an essential task for quantum sensing and computation. Extensive theoretical work indicates that these capabilities can enable dynamical phases and critical phenomena that show topologically robust methods to create, protect and manipulate quantum entanglement that self-correct against large classes of errors. However, so far, experimental realizations have been confined to classical (non-entangled) symmetry-breaking orders 1-5 . In this work, we demonstrate an emergent dynamical symmetry-protected topological phase 6 , in a quasiperiodically driven array of ten 171 Yb + hyperfine qubits in Quantinuum's System Model H1 trapped-ion quantum processor 7 . This phase shows edge qubits that are dynamically protected from control errors, cross-talk and stray fields. Crucially, this edge protection relies purely on emergent dynamical symmetries that are absolutely stable to generic coherent perturbations. This property is special to quasiperiodically driven systems: as we demonstrate, the analogous edge states of a periodically driven qubit array are vulnerable to symmetry-breaking errors and quickly decohere. Our work paves the way for implementation of more complex dynamical topological orders 8,9 that would enable error-resilient manipulation of quantum information.

# Digital quantum simulation of Floquet symmetry-protected topological phases
## Abstract
Here we report the observation of a distinct type of non-equilibrium state of matter, Floquet symmetry-protected topological phases, which are implemented through digital quantum simulation with an array of programmable superconducting qubits.
We observe robust long-lived temporal correlations and subharmonic temporal response for the edge spins over up to 40 driving cycles using a circuit of depth exceeding 240 and acting on 26 qubits.
We demonstrate that the subharmonic response is independent of the initial state, and experimentally map out a phase boundary between the Floquet symmetry-protected topological and thermal phases.
...
## Symmetry breaking at boundaries
From Fig. 2a, it is evident that in the FSPT phase, the disorder-averaged magnetizations at the two ends of the chain, namely \(\overline{\langle {\sigma }_{1}^{z}(t)\rangle }\) and \(\overline{\langle {\sigma }_{L}^{z}(t)\rangle }\), oscillate with a 2*T* periodicity, for up to 40 driving cycles.
In stark contrast, the local magnetizations in the bulk of the chain (\(\overline{\langle {\sigma }_{j}^{z}(t)\rangle }\) with \(2\le j\le L-1\)) decay quickly to zero and do not show period-doubled oscillations.
...
For comparison, we also experimentally measure the dynamics of the magnetizations in the thermal phase.
Our results are shown in Fig. 2c,e, where we see that the magnetizations for both the edge and bulk spins decay quickly to zero and no subharmonic response appears at all.
...

We measured the persistent oscillations of edge spins with a subharmonic frequency and experimentally demonstrated that the FSPT phases are robust to symmetry-respecting perturbations in the drive and imperfections in the experiment.

Our preparation relies on simultaneous control over an array of tightly focused individual addressing laser beams, generating long-range spin–spin interactions.
We also observe a disordered phase with frustrated correlations.

paper.title: Dynamical topological phase realized in a trapped-ion quantum simulator.
paper.authors: Dumitrescu PT, Bohnet JG, Gaebler JP, Hankin A, Hayes D, Kumar A, Neyenhuis B, Vasseur R, Potter AC.
paper.abstract: Nascent platforms for programmable quantum simulation offer unprecedented access to new regimes of far-from-equilibrium quantum many-body dynamics in almost isolated systems. Here achieving precise control over quantum many-body entanglement is an essential task for quantum sensing and computation. Extensive theoretical work indicates that these capabilities can enable dynamical phases and critical phenomena that show topologically robust methods to create, protect and manipulate quantum entanglement that self-correct against large classes of errors. However, so far, experimental realizations have been confined to classical (non-entangled) symmetry-breaking orders 1-5 . In this work, we demonstrate an emergent dynamical symmetry-protected topological phase 6 , in a quasiperiodically driven array of ten 171 Yb + hyperfine qubits in Quantinuum's System Model H1 trapped-ion quantum processor 7 . This phase shows edge qubits that are dynamically protected from control errors, cross-talk and stray fields. Crucially, this edge protection relies purely on emergent dynamical symmetries that are absolutely stable to generic coherent perturbations. This property is special to quasiperiodically driven systems: as we demonstrate, the analogous edge states of a periodically driven qubit array are vulnerable to symmetry-breaking errors and quickly decohere. Our work paves the way for implementation of more complex dynamical topological orders 8,9 that would enable error-resilient manipulation of quantum information.

# Digital quantum simulation of Floquet symmetry-protected topological phases
## Abstract
Here we report the observation of a distinct type of non-equilibrium state of matter, Floquet symmetry-protected topological phases, which are implemented through digital quantum simulation with an array of programmable superconducting qubits.
We observe robust long-lived temporal correlations and subharmonic temporal response for the edge spins over up to 40 driving cycles using a circuit of depth exceeding 240 and acting on 26 qubits.
